DONE (s470bq, Opus, 2026-09-05).  ir-spec Â§5.1's facts table gained the row.

`p-sub`'s facts plist gains `:needs (CLASSESâ¦)`: the obligation classes the
sub's BODY exercises, spelled with Â§10b's own class names
(`:nonlocal_exit.die`, `:dynamic_scope.local`, `:io`, `:regex.native` â¦) so
the per-sub and per-program answers cannot drift.

IT IS THE ONE KEY THAT IS A COMPLETE ANSWER rather than a proof-if-present, so
it is ALWAYS printed, possibly `()`.  That is the point: the ABSENCE is what a
target uses -- nothing can throw, so no frame; nothing localizes, so no
save/restore stack (plan Â§B.3's table); and a backend can compile a program
PARTIALLY, taking every sub whose classes it implements and refusing the rest
with Â§9.3b's shape.

MECHANISM: `Pl::Manifest`'s walk was made REENTRANT (every count lives in an
accumulator the walk is handed) and `needs_of_form` walks ONE sub body into a
fresh accumulator.  Same table, same walk, two scopes -- the alternative was a
second walk with its own copy of %OBLIGATION, which is the drift rule 11
forbids.  `*p-sub-fact-keys*` in the runtime gained `:needs` (the set is
closed at both ends).

Cost: one walk of the body the emitter has just built, no second
representation.
